precepts.text: Do what? Flee also youthful lust. The Bible says, "Flee also youthful lusts, but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart." Go back to 3 and 6. Now.
precepts.point: For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women. Silly women, laden with sins. Stop. What scripture will we go back to for that? Read it again. I forgot. Go back. Go back. Go back. Verse 22. Go back. Come on, y'all. Stay with me, y'all. The topic has not changed. Come on. Verse 22 of chapter 2.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

precepts.why:
“For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” To understand who these are, go back to chapter 2, verse 22, because this is one long letter and the topic has not changed: “Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.”

The men of the last days are “lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy”, without natural affection toward their brothers and sisters, trucebreakers, false accusers. Incontinent means you are all over the place: no guideline, no law, no discipline. Fierce means angry. Traitors, heady, high-minded, “lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.”

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof.” Who is that? Israel, and more specifically the vessels of dishonour, the wood and the earth. You have a form of godliness, but you deny the laws of God; you follow no law. “from such turn away.” Not entertain them: turn away. God says turn away from those brothers that are dishonourable, the wood and the earth, and leave them the hell alone. In meekness you instruct those that oppose themselves, that “they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will”, but you do not walk with them.

These are the men who did not flee youthful lusts. They creep into houses and lead captive silly women: you get a silly woman who just came into the body and doesn’t know a damn thing, you crop yourself next to her and say you are her counselor now, I’m going to counsel you, sister, I got you. And she is laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.

So flee youthful lusts, and follow righteousness, faith, charity and peace with those that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. That is what separates the gold and silver from the wood and the earth. The precious sons of Zion are “comparable to fine gold”, and God said it, not man; but youthful lusts have turned the gold dim and made us earthen pitchers.

precepts.text: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness. If any of you have ever dealt with us in a counsel setting, where are we going to read from? The scriptures. And your anger, your disdain, is not with us, it is with God. So when you get that deep sinking feeling in your diaphragm, when you want to get upset, want to get mad, that is Satan stirring you up to be disobedient to what God has said.
precepts.point: For this cause, when I could no longer forbear, I sent to know your faith, lest by some means the tempter have tempted you, and our labour be in vain. So he is telling the congregation in Thessalonica that during the afflictions the tempter is going to tempt you. Christ was tempted after his forty days and forty nights of fasting, in a weakened state. During the afflictions we are mentally, probably physically, spiritually in a weakened state. The tempter is going to tempt you. And then our labour is in vain, because we have been here teaching Christ this entire time, and now because of the afflictions you say, we are not going to follow Christ any more, we are going to go back to animal sacrifice. That is part of the tempter tempting you.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.why:
Paul sent to know the Thessalonians’ faith “lest by some means the tempter have tempted you, and our labour be in vain.” During afflictions we are mentally, physically and spiritually in a weakened state, as Christ was after forty days and forty nights of fasting, and the tempter comes. One of the ways he comes is through correction. When tribulation comes, brothers who do not want to address the elephant in the room leave and rebrand themselves, like the brother who was here in 2016 and 2017, never around long enough to be built up, now online as an apologist calling himself an ex black Hebrew Israelite. He could not get his wife to submit, and rather than take the counsel, he left.

“All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.” If you have ever dealt with us in a counsel setting, where are we going to read from? The scriptures. So your anger and your disdain is not with us; it is with God.

When you get that deep sinking feeling in your diaphragm, when you want to get upset and get mad, that is Satan stirring you up to be disobedient to what God has said, using your emotions to unravel you. Whether it is correction or instruction in righteousness, such as, brother, I do not think this move is good for you, do not go down this path, some brothers get in their feelings and do what they want anyway. Then the hands of the one who gave the instruction are clear.

Counsel is of the Lord, and the Lord is in the midst of it. But Satan is right there too, telling you it is not of the Lord. Stay in the spirit, so that the tempter does not make the labour in vain.

precepts.text: This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof. You know why it says a form of godliness? That is the fringes and the border of blue, walking around with your Bible saying all the greetings, but you are really not keeping the commandments in your heart. From such turn away: the same thing he said in the chapter before, purge yourself from these.
precepts.point: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work. When you purge a plant you are pruning it, taking away the bad elements. Likewise with us: the bad elements among us, you have to cut off. I knew which brothers I always used to get in trouble with; I had to cut them off and hang out with leadership.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Paul says in a great house there are vessels “of gold and of silver” and also “of wood and of earth”, and “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour.” The next chapter names who those vessels of dishonour are: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.”

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof.” Why does it say a form of godliness? That is the fringes everybody wears and the border of blue, walking around with your Bible, saying Most High, in Christ, blessed heartily. But you are not keeping the laws in your heart. You are really not keeping the commandments.

The great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation of Israel. There are brothers and sisters of gold and silver, applying what we read in 1 Peter 2:1-2. And there are brothers and sisters with fringes and a border of blue who are no damn good. They have not changed their lives; they are the same as they were two, three years ago. Not the new people who just came in, but people who have been with us for years and are still grimy: still that secret adulterer, that liar, complainer, murmurer. You are that wood and that earth. In every IUIC school there are men and women of honour and of dishonour, and the captains must be able to identify which is which. If you can’t do that, there is a problem.

“from such turn away.” That is what he said in the chapter before: purge yourself from these. Purge means cut them off, cut them loose. When you purge a plant you are pruning it, taking away the bad elements. Likewise with us: the bad elements among us, you have to cut off. You know which brothers always get you in trouble. Rolling with grimy brothers, you can almost get arrested many a time; cut them off, say I’m not rolling with y’all no more, and hang out with leadership. That is how you become a vessel “sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.”

precepts.text: For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts. Fasting was meant to curb the desires; not with these men.
precepts.point: Not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: other translations read, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying, and sacrificing, yet they were still sexually indulgent all over the place. When it came to satisfying the flesh, they had no honor.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
The end of Colossians 2:23, “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh”, seems like hard wording. Other translations read it, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying and sacrificing, and they were still sexually indulgent all over the place: spiritual discipline, worldly desires, spiritual discipline, temptation, over and over.

Timothy describes that same sort: “For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts”. He is talking about these scribes and Pharisees, these type of men.

I thought fasting was meant to curb your desires. Not with these men. It inflamed their desires. They showed humility and neglected the body with fasting, and they still crept into houses to lead silly women captive. That is what Paul means by no honour to the satisfying of the flesh.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.
precepts.point: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. It is going to happen; it is inevitable. Remember Ecclesiasticus 2: my son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. You caught hell coming into this truth; Satan did not want to let you go. Old acquaintances from years ago suddenly contacting you: Satan wanted you. He does not want one of us to wake up. But we are here.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” It is just a part of being in this truth. All of you went through it; you don’t even have to be asked. You caught hell coming into this truth. That is just how it works.

Satan didn’t want to let you go. He didn’t want to give you up. You had family, you had old hoes contacting you from years ago: how did you get my number? Satan. Satan wanted you. He doesn’t want a single one of us to wake up. But we are here.

That is why Paul says “all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” It is going to happen; you are going to go through things; it is inevitable. “For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.” There are going to be schisms and divisions and things happening amongst us, all to find out who is built for the battle and who is going to make it through. Is a confrontation with a sister you keep bumping heads with going to take you out? Your marijuana addiction, your addiction to women, your addiction to porn? Or are you going to fight the fight and keep throwing blows back while you are getting hit? As long as you are fighting you are all right; the moment you stop fighting, it is over.

Pressure either bursts pipes or it doesn’t. Pressure exposes the weak points, and then you see where the repairs need to be made. And some go through heavy things, a husband who did this and that, and they are still here, strong as hell. Christ said “It is impossible but that offences will come.” Somebody is going to disappoint you, misunderstand you, correct you, overlook you, frustrate you. You didn’t run away from home over a fight with your sibling; you stayed, and you didn’t stop loving them. We are in the trenches, and we are not leaving. Prepare your soul for it, because the temptation is part of coming to serve the Lord.

precepts.text: This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves: going for likes and followers, me, me, me, when it is not about you, it is about your people. Covetous, boasters of vanity, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, without natural affection: this is the nature of them that go after the world, after the gift that destroys the heart.
precepts.point: We live in an era where vanity and attention are a drug. At the outreach last week, the kids all said they want to be streamers. What about a plumber, a mechanic, a builder, an architect, a lawyer, an engineer: the things that actually build nations? That is part of why we have been destroyed as a people.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
“This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.” In perilous times we have to start having all things in common, like the believers of Acts 4, and build our faith.

“For men shall be lovers of their own selves”: going for likes, not worried about being an aid to your society or your community. It is me, me, me: how many likes and followers do I have? It is not about you, negro. It is about your people. “Covetous, boasters”: boasting of vanity, money, drugs, houses, cars, women. “Proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful”: not appreciative of God and what he has done for you. “Unholy, Without natural affection”.

This is the nature of them that go after the world, that go after the gift that destroys the heart. The one who is a lover of himself holds on to what he has; the believers in Acts 4 said none of the things they possessed was their own.

So we have to stop living beyond our means and be content with our wages and content in life. A family of seven may need a house with a little room, but if you are a single brother, why are you buying a mansion and expensive cars? Do you know the times we are living in? There is coming a time when you will not be worrying about maintaining your BMW. Riches and comfort, keeping up with the Joneses and the American lie of a dream, should not be your god.

precepts.text: You cannot accuse, you cannot blame, until you have seen all that needs to be seen concerning a matter. You look foolish when you do this without understanding what's going on. Your opinion, if it lacks understanding, if it lacks the pertinent information that needs to be used in order to explain what's going on, but you feel necessary to give that opinion, something is wrong with you. You've been put in many situations that have shown you: yeah, you jumped the gun. But yet and still, you feel your opinion matters. It don't. Understand first, and then rebuke.
precepts.point: That's the type of people you don't know for exhorting anybody. You only know them for bringing problems about everything they see, but they lack exhortation in any form.

note.label: Jude 1:16

precepts.why:
We were warned: “in the last days perilous times shall come”, and among the men of those days are “false accusers.” Sirach gives the law against it: “Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.”

You cannot accuse, you cannot blame, until you have seen all that needs to be seen concerning a matter. How many people run their mouth without understanding, without knowing? How many gossip without the full understanding of what is going on, yet have so many opinions and thoughts on how this should be, on what so-and-so is doing and shouldn’t be doing? You look foolish when you do this without understanding what is going on.

If your opinion lacks understanding, if it lacks the pertinent information needed to explain what is going on, but you still feel it necessary to give it, something is wrong with you. You have been put in many situations that showed you that you jumped the gun, that you didn’t know what was going on. Yet and still you feel your opinion matters. It doesn’t. Understand first, and then rebuke.

That goes with the pride Paul names. The prideful spirit won’t allow you to take any correction or accept what is being said; it has you thinking it is everybody but you. And it goes with the “despisers of those that are good”: people who hate that you are doing what you are supposed to do, that you are above them in rank and active in the body. Every time you turn around they have a suggestion nobody asked for, and they don’t say it to you; they tell everybody underneath you, so all your peers know how they feel. You never know them for exhorting anybody, only for bringing problems about everything they see.

The law says “Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people.” The talebearer with the tea, who somehow knows before leadership knows, is the fuel that keeps reputations scarred and people at odds. And when you tell a story as if you know what is going on, without the whole story, and it is not true, that is a lie: “he that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight.” That is why you must examine the truth before you blame.

precepts.text: As Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth, men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith; but they shall proceed no further, for their folly shall be manifest unto all. It is clear we do not tithe with no temple and clear there are no multiple wives in 1 Corinthians 7; resist that and the mind corrupts.
precepts.point: Nobody questions these men because the souls following them are unstable and cannot go to the book and study to show themselves approved. An heart exercised with covetous practices, cursed children, which have forsaken the right way. The right way is to keep the commandments without adding an alternate reality to fit what you want.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
Only people that don't study get caught up in this foolishness. You can hear people in the crowd agreeing: yeah, oh man. But Paul says: “Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth”. It isn't just him; it is all those that resist the truth, and you will see it over and over.

Why do these dumb doctrines and silly sayings come out? They are “men of corrupt minds”, because they have resisted the truth. It is clear we don't tithe anymore; the temple is not there. It is clear you don't have multiple wives; you read that in 1 Corinthians 7. But they resist the truth, and now their minds are corrupt, and you hear about innie and Audi and all the rest.

They are “reprobate concerning the faith”: these men are not in the faith. They don't believe, and those who get caught up with them are in the same boat. “But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs also was.” They will not go any further. Their folly is being made manifest among all men, and that is why they will have to fix their face.

precepts.text: In the last days men shall be lovers of their own selves, without natural affection (minors, the same sex), trucebreakers, despisers of those that are good (I just don't like that brother; what does he do? teach the word of God), traitors, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God. Love pleasure more than God and you make excuses to feed the lust and stop showing up for the work.
precepts.point: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. Many of you see America as a gorgeous woman and are mesmerized; every pleasure is available in her. Many brothers fall by harlots, and you do not have to pick up a prostitute to be dealing with the mother of all harlots.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.” Many of you look at America as a gorgeous, beautiful woman, and you are mesmerized. In America you can have every kind of pleasure. A lot of brothers fall by harlots, and just because you are not picking up a prostitute doesn’t mean you aren’t out there dealing with harlots. This is the mother of all harlots. And remember, sin is pleasurable.

Paul describes the last days: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection”: some like young minors, some like people of the same sex. “Trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good.” I don’t like that brother. Why not? Every time I look up he is doing something. What, teaching the word of God? We have spirits like that sitting among us, worried about petty things while this truth is trying to get us out of here.

“Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.” That is a big issue. If you love pleasure more than you love God, you start making excuses to feed that lust, and you find yourself not around doing the Lord’s work as much. Everybody asks, what’s wrong with that brother’s spirit? He loves his lust more than God.

That is what it means to stumble at the beauty of the woman and desire her for pleasure: to love America’s pleasures more than God. The brothers and sisters who fade away, this is your gut check.

precepts.text: Know how to behave in the house of God, the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.
precepts.point: We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels, constrained from sin.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation”. Paul tells Timothy where that comes from: “But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.”

The holy scriptures make you wise unto salvation, the very wisdom that is the stability of thy times and the strength of salvation. We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must know how to behave in the house of God. Continue in the things you have learned, knowing of whom you learned them, and learn to behave yourselves and possess your vessels.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: How far our people the Israelites have gone. “In the last days”: the last days are today’s days. “Lovers of their own selves”: when you hear somebody say me, me, me, that’s a lover of self. “Covetous”: give me, pay me. “Unthankful”: before we came into this truth we were all grimy, but when the Lord brought men into our lives to teach us who we are, some of us became unthankful. “Without natural affection”: you thought brothers and sisters were your friends, but money was the friend. “Lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God”: money is good, but when it becomes your god there is a problem. “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”: they learned the scriptures, but what the law says, they reject. “From such turn away”: when you meet men and women like that, leave them alone. Clear out your Facebook friends and start again.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come
